## What it is

The Configuration Management policy states what the organization requires for configuration management and who is accountable for it. It meets [CM-1](/controls/cm/cm-1/) through the sections every family policy shares, and adds one statement group per control. Each baseline variant includes only the controls in that baseline, taken from the NIST SP 800-53B profiles.

Adopt the ready-to-adopt edition: fill every highlighted field, delete any "Federal systems" section that does not apply, and have the accountable official approve it. The annotated edition adds guidance on why each section exists and what assessors look for.

## Decisions to make first

The policy has 74 organization-defined parameters across all variants; each appears as a highlighted field with its typical value where one is given. Settle these first:

| Decision | Controls | Typical | Who decides |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Which published secure configurations does each component type start from? | [CM-6](/controls/cm/cm-6/) | Vendor security baselines or checklists from the NIST National Checklist Program, tailored in the baseline configuration standard. | Chief Information Security Officer |
| Who sits on the change control board, and which changes may skip it? | [CM-3](/controls/cm/cm-3/), [CM-3(4)](/controls/cm/cm-3/#cm-3.4) | The system owner, technical leads and a security representative; preapproved standard changes and emergency changes reviewed after the fact. | System owner |
| Which tool is the authoritative component inventory? | [CM-8](/controls/cm/cm-8/), [CM-8(2)](/controls/cm/cm-8/#cm-8.2) | The asset discovery or endpoint management tool, reconciled with the system inventory. | Chief Information Security Officer |

Record your values in the [Configuration Management decision worksheet](/templates/worksheets/cm/), which lists every parameter with its typical value.

## Preview (Moderate baseline, annotated)

:::note[Guidance]
The sections before and after Policy statements meet CM-1, which asks for a policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination and compliance, plus procedures, dissemination, a designated official and a review cycle. Assessors check each element, so keep every section even when it is short. Each statement cites the CM-1 item it meets. If you adopt several family policies, the same sections repeat in each; that is expected, and it lets each policy stand alone.
:::

### Purpose

This policy states what <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> requires for Configuration Management, and who is accountable for meeting those requirements. (CM-1a.1(a))

### Scope

This policy applies at the <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: organization-level; mission/business process-level; system-level</span> to every system that <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span> owns or operates, or that is operated on its behalf, and to every person with access to those systems, including employees, contractors and partners. (CM-1a.1(a))

### Roles and responsibilities

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> is accountable for this policy and shall approve exceptions to it. (CM-1a.1(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the configuration management policy and procedures</span> shall manage the development, documentation and dissemination of this policy and its procedures. (CM-1b)
- Each <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement this policy for their system and document how in the system security plan. (CM-1a.1(a))
- Each person within scope shall follow this policy and report suspected violations to the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>. (CM-1a.1(a))

### Management commitment

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Senior leader</span> approves this policy and shall provide the resources needed to implement it. (CM-1a.1(a))

### Coordination

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall coordinate this policy with the legal, privacy, human resources and procurement functions, and with the owners of related policies, before each approval. (CM-1a.1(a))

### Compliance

- This policy shall be consistent with the laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards and guidelines that apply to <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Organization name</span>, including <span class="tpl-field tpl-fill">Fill in: laws, regulations and standards that apply to the organization</span>. (CM-1a.1(b))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall review compliance with this policy through the organization's assessment and continuous monitoring activities. (CM-1a.1(a))
- An exception to this policy shall be requested in writing, approved by the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span>, time-limited and recorded with its compensating measures. (CM-1a.1(a))
- Violations of this policy shall be handled through the organization's sanctions process. (CM-1a.1(a))

### Procedures

The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the configuration management policy and procedures</span> shall ensure that documented procedures exist to implement this policy and its associated controls. (CM-1a.2)

### Dissemination

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the configuration management policy and procedures</span> shall disseminate this policy to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to whom the configuration management policy is to be disseminated</span>. (CM-1a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the configuration management policy and procedures</span> shall disseminate the procedures that implement this policy to <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to whom the configuration management procedures are to be disseminated</span>. (CM-1a)

### Policy statements

:::note[Guidance]
Each statement below comes from the clause for one control or enhancement in the chosen baseline. The reference at the end of each statement names the control item it meets.
:::

#### Baseline configuration (CM-2)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall develop, document and maintain under configuration control a current baseline configuration of the system. (CM-2a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall review and update the baseline configuration <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency of baseline configuration review and update <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at least annually</span></span>. (CM-2b.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall review and update the baseline configuration when required by <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the circumstances requiring baseline configuration review and update <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: a significant change to the system, a new version of the secure configuration it is based on, or a security incident</span></span>. (CM-2b.2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall review and update the baseline configuration when system components are installed or upgraded. (CM-2b.3)

#### Automation support for accuracy and currency (CM-2(2))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall maintain the currency, completeness, accuracy and availability of the baseline configuration using <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: automated mechanisms for maintaining baseline configuration of the system <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: configuration management and infrastructure-as-code tools that record the approved baseline</span></span>. (CM-2(2))

#### Retention of previous configurations (CM-2(3))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall retain <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the number of previous baseline configuration versions to be retained <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at least the two most recent</span></span> previous versions of the baseline configuration to support rollback. (CM-2(3))

#### Configure systems and components for high-risk areas (CM-2(7))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall ensure individuals traveling to locations the organization deems to be of significant risk are issued <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the systems or system components to be issued when individuals travel to high-risk areas <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: loaner laptops and mobile devices</span></span> with <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: configurations for systems or system components to be issued when individuals travel to high-risk areas <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: a minimal configuration with full-disk encryption, no stored organizational data and access only through the organization's VPN</span></span>. (CM-2(7)(a))
- When those individuals return, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall ensure the following controls are applied to the devices: <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the controls to be applied when the individuals return from travel <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: inspecting the device, wiping and reimaging it before reuse, and resetting the user's credentials</span></span>. (CM-2(7)(b))

#### Configuration change control (CM-3)

:::note[Guidance]
CM-3 is where most programs either show discipline or show a gap. Keep one change record per change, with the request, the impact analysis (CM-4), the decision, the test result and the implementation date. Assessors sample changes from the system and trace each back to an approved record.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall determine and document the types of changes to the system that are configuration-controlled. (CM-3a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall review proposed configuration-controlled changes and approve or disapprove them with explicit consideration of security and privacy impact analyses. (CM-3b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall document configuration change decisions for the system. (CM-3c)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement only approved configuration-controlled changes. (CM-3d)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall retain records of configuration-controlled changes for <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the time period to retain records of configuration-controlled changes <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at least one year, or the life of the system if longer</span></span>. (CM-3e)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall monitor and review activities associated with configuration-controlled changes. (CM-3f)
- Configuration change control activities shall be coordinated and overseen by <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the configuration change control element responsible for coordinating and overseeing change control activities <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: a change control board with the system owner, technical leads and a security representative</span></span>, which convenes <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] ; when [Assignment: organization-defined configuration change conditions]  <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: weekly, and when an emergency change is requested</span></span>. (CM-3g)

#### Testing, validation and documentation of changes (CM-3(2))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall test, validate and document changes before finalizing their implementation. (CM-3(2))

#### Security and privacy representatives (CM-3(4))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall require <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: security and privacy representatives <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: a representative of the security team and, where the system processes personal information, of the privacy office</span></span> to be members of <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the configuration change control element of which the security and privacy representatives are to be members <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the change control board</span></span>. (CM-3(4))

#### Impact analyses (CM-4)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall analyze changes to the system to determine potential security and privacy impacts before the changes are implemented. (CM-4)

#### Verification of controls (CM-4(2))

- After a system change, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall verify that the impacted controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended and producing the desired outcome. (CM-4(2))

#### Access restrictions for change (CM-5)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall define, document, approve and enforce physical and logical access restrictions associated with changes to the system. (CM-5)

#### Configuration settings (CM-6)

:::note[Guidance]
Pick a published secure configuration for each component type rather than writing your own: vendor security baselines and checklists from the NIST National Checklist Program ([SP 800-70 Rev. 5](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/70/r5/final), May 2026) are common starting points. Record each deviation with its reason and approval; assessors compare scan results against the baseline and ask for the approval of every difference.
:::

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall establish and document configuration settings for system components that reflect the most restrictive mode consistent with operational requirements, using <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: common secure configurations to establish and document configuration settings for components employed within the system <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the secure configuration baselines named in the baseline configuration standard</span></span>. (CM-6a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall implement the configuration settings. (CM-6b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall identify, document and approve any deviation from the established settings for <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: system components for which approval of deviations is needed <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: all system components</span></span>, based on <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: operational requirements necessitating approval of deviations <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: documented operational needs that the system owner approves and the security team reviews</span></span>. (CM-6c)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall monitor and control changes to the configuration settings in accordance with this policy and its procedures. (CM-6d)

#### Least functionality (CM-7)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall configure the system to provide only <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: mission-essential capabilities for the system <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the capabilities documented in the system security plan</span></span>. (CM-7a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall prohibit or restrict the use of <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: prohibited or restricted functions, system ports, protocols, software, and/or services <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the functions, ports, protocols, software and services listed as prohibited or restricted in the baseline configuration standard</span></span>. (CM-7b)

#### Periodic review (CM-7(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall review the system <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which to review the system to identify unnecessary and/or non-secure functions, ports, protocols, software, and/or services <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at least quarterly</span></span> to identify unnecessary or nonsecure functions, ports, protocols, software and services. (CM-7(1)(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall disable or remove <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: functions, ports, protocols, software, and services within the system deemed to be unnecessary and/or nonsecure <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: any function, port, protocol, software or service the review finds unnecessary or nonsecure</span></span>. (CM-7(1)(b))

#### Prevent program execution (CM-7(2))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the system prevents program execution in accordance with <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: [Assignment: organization-defined policies, rules of behavior, and/or access agreements regarding software program usage and restrictions] ; rules authorizing the terms and conditions of software program usage <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the software rules in this policy, the rules of behavior and the access agreements</span></span>. (CM-7(2))

#### Authorized software: allow by exception (CM-7(5))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall identify <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: software programs authorized to execute on the system <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the software on the approved software list for the system</span></span> as the software programs authorized to execute on the system. (CM-7(5)(a))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall employ a deny-all, permit-by-exception policy to allow only authorized software programs to execute. (CM-7(5)(b))
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall review and update the list of authorized software programs <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: frequency at which to review and update the list of authorized software programs <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at least quarterly</span></span>. (CM-7(5)(c))

#### System component inventory (CM-8)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall develop and document an inventory of system components that accurately reflects the system and includes all its components. (CM-8a.1, a.2)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the inventory has no duplicate accounting of components and no components assigned to another system. (CM-8a.3)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the inventory is at the level of granularity needed for tracking and reporting. (CM-8a.4)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the inventory includes <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: information deemed necessary to achieve effective system component accountability <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: name, type, manufacturer and model, serial number or asset tag, software version, location, network address, owner and administrator</span></span> for each component. (CM-8a.5)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall review and update the inventory <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: frequency at which to review and update the system component inventory <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at least quarterly</span></span>. (CM-8b)

#### Updates during installation and removal (CM-8(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall update the component inventory as part of component installations, removals and system updates. (CM-8(1))

#### Automated unauthorized component detection (CM-8(3))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall detect the presence of unauthorized hardware, software and firmware components using <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: automated mechanisms <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: network access control, asset discovery scans and endpoint management tools</span></span> <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: frequency at which automated mechanisms are used to detect the presence of unauthorized system components within the system <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: continuously, and at least weekly by scan</span></span>. (CM-8(3)(a))
- When unauthorized components are detected, the <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Select one or more: disable network access by unauthorized components; isolate unauthorized components; notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]  <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: disable network access by unauthorized components, and notify the security operations team</span></span>. (CM-8(3)(b))

#### Configuration management plan (CM-9)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall develop, document and implement a configuration management plan for the system that addresses roles, responsibilities, and configuration management processes and procedures. (CM-9a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the plan establishes a process for identifying configuration items throughout the system development life cycle and for managing their configuration. (CM-9b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall ensure the plan defines the configuration items for the system and places them under configuration management. (CM-9c)
- The plan shall be reviewed and approved by <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: personnel or roles to review and approve the configuration management plan <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the system owner and the Chief Information Security Officer</span></span>. (CM-9d)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall protect the plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification. (CM-9e)

#### Software usage restrictions (CM-10)

- Users shall use software and its documentation in accordance with contract agreements and copyright laws. (CM-10a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall track the use of software and documentation protected by quantity licenses to control copying and distribution. (CM-10b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall control and document the use of peer-to-peer file sharing technology so that it is not used for unauthorized distribution, display, performance or reproduction of copyrighted work. (CM-10c)

#### User-installed software (CM-11)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">Chief Information Security Officer</span> shall establish the following rules for software installation by users: <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: policies governing the installation of software by users <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: users may install only software from the organization's approved software catalog; all other installation requires approval by the system owner</span></span>. (CM-11a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall enforce those rules through <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: methods used to enforce software installation policies <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: removing local administrator rights and using an application allow list</span></span>. (CM-11b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall monitor compliance with those rules <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: frequency with which to monitor compliance <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: at least monthly</span></span>. (CM-11c)

#### Information location (CM-12)

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall identify and document the location of <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: information for which the location is to be identified and documented <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: the information types listed in the system security plan</span></span> and the specific components on which it is processed and stored. (CM-12a)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall identify and document the users who have access to the system and components where that information is processed and stored. (CM-12b)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall document changes to the location where that information is processed and stored. (CM-12c)

#### Automated tools to support information location (CM-12(1))

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-org">System owner</span> shall use automated tools to identify <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: information to be protected is defined by information type <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: personal information and other sensitive information types listed in the system security plan</span></span> on <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: system components where the information is located <span class="tpl-typical">Typical: file shares, databases, cloud storage and endpoints</span></span> to confirm controls are in place to protect organizational information and individual privacy. (CM-12(1))

### Review and update

- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the configuration management policy and procedures</span> shall review and update this policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which the current configuration management policy is reviewed and updated</span> and following <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that would require the current configuration management policy to be reviewed and updated</span>. (CM-1c.1)
- The <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: an official to manage the configuration management policy and procedures</span> shall review and update the procedures that implement this policy <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: the frequency at which the current configuration management procedures are reviewed and updated</span> and following <span class="tpl-field tpl-param">Fill in: events that would require configuration management procedures to be reviewed and updated</span>. (CM-1c.2)

<div class="tpl-federal">

#### Federal systems

For federal information systems, this policy also carries out the agency's information security responsibilities under the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 ([44 U.S.C. § 3554](https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title44-section3554&num=0&edition=prelim), Federal agency responsibilities) and [OMB Circular A-130](https://www.whitehouse.gov/wp-content/uploads/legacy_drupal_files/omb/circulars/A130/a130revised.pdf), Appendix I, Responsibilities for Protecting and Managing Federal Information Resources.

- Where the agency's organization-wide policy sets a value for a parameter in this policy, each system shall use that value or a stricter one. (CM-1a.1(b))

</div>
